questions.question: What are the four main principles of composition discussed in the lecture?
questions.explanation: The four main principles of composition are Proximity, Alignment, Repetition, and Contrast. These principles help create effective visual designs.

questions.question: According to the principle of proximity, what does physical closeness imply?
questions.explanation: The principle of proximity states that physical closeness implies a relationship. Group related items together and separate items that are not related.

questions.question: What box model properties can help you create proximity and alignment?
questions.explanation: Padding and margin are box model properties that control spacing around elements. Margin creates space between elements (proximity), while padding creates space inside elements. Both can be used to create alignment and control the visual relationships between elements.

questions.question: For contrast to be effective, what must it be?
questions.explanation: For contrast to be effective, it must be strong and bold. Contrast can be created through size, color (cool v. warm), whitespace, or asymmetry.

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of the U.S. population has some form of a disability?
questions.explanation: Approximately 26% of the U.S. population has some form of a disability. This makes accessibility a critical consideration in web design.

questions.question: What legal precedent established that the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) applies to websites?
questions.explanation: The Domino's Pizza ruling established that the ADA applies to websites, making inaccessibility potentially illegal.

questions.question: What is the standard for web accessibility?
questions.explanation: WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) is the set of standards for web accessibility. There are plenty of accessibility resources available to help you get started.

questions.question: What should you always set for a webpage to improve accessibility?
questions.explanation: You should always set the language of a webpage (e.g., <html lang="en">) to improve accessibility, especially for screen readers.

questions.question: Why is semantic HTML important for accessibility?
options: It provides meaning and structure that screen readers can understand
questions.explanation: Semantic HTML provides meaning and structure that screen readers and other assistive technologies can understand, making content more accessible to users with disabilities.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the alt attribute on images?
options: To provide a tooltip when hovering over the image
To provide alternative text that describes the image for screen readers and when images fail to load
To specify the image file path
questions.explanation: The alt attribute provides alternative text that describes the image. This is essential for screen readers to convey image content to blind users, and it's also displayed when images fail to load.

questions.question: What should you do if an image is purely decorative and doesn't convey important information?
options: Use the filename as alt text
questions.explanation: For decorative images that don't convey important information, you should use an empty alt attribute (alt=""). This tells screen readers to skip the image, preventing unnecessary announcements.

questions.question: Why is keyboard navigation important for accessibility?
options: It makes websites faster to use
Many users with mobility disabilities cannot use a mouse and rely on keyboard navigation
questions.explanation: Keyboard navigation is essential because many users with mobility disabilities cannot use a mouse and rely entirely on keyboard navigation. All interactive elements must be keyboard accessible.

questions.question: What does ARIA stand for and what is its purpose?
options: Accessible Rich Internet Applications - provides additional semantic information for assistive technologies
Automated Responsive Interface Attributes - makes pages responsive
Advanced Responsive Internet Applications - improves performance
Accessible Responsive Internet Attributes - handles mobile layouts
questions.explanation: ARIA stands for Accessible Rich Internet Applications. It provides additional semantic information through attributes that help assistive technologies understand and interact with web content, especially for dynamic content.

questions.question: What should you use for descriptive links to improve accessibility?
questions.explanation: You should use descriptive links (e.g., 'accessibility resources') rather than generic text like 'more info here' or 'click here' to improve accessibility, especially for screen readers.

questions.question: What can the WAVE browser extension help you check? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The WAVE browser extension can help check many accessibility issues including missing alt text, color contrast problems, missing form labels, heading structure issues, keyboard navigation problems, and missing language attributes. It's a comprehensive accessibility testing tool.

questions.question: What is the purpose of heading hierarchy (h1, h2, h3, etc.) for accessibility?
options: To provide document structure that screen readers can navigate
questions.explanation: Heading hierarchy provides document structure that screen readers can use to navigate. Users can jump between headings to quickly understand and navigate the page structure, similar to a table of contents.

questions.question: What is the purpose of captions and transcripts for video and audio content?
options: To make content accessible to deaf and hard-of-hearing users, as well as users in noisy environments
questions.explanation: Captions and transcripts make audio and video content accessible to deaf and hard-of-hearing users. They're also helpful for users in noisy environments, users learning a language, and for SEO purposes.

questions.question: What should you avoid when designing for users with color blindness?
options: Relying solely on color to convey important information
questions.explanation: You should avoid relying solely on color to convey important information. Instead, use additional indicators like icons, text labels, or patterns. For example, don't just use red/green to indicate errors/success - also include text or icons.
